editor_note: The page is faithful overall and the casual Taglish register holds, with no po/opo. In entry [3], "done consistently and correctly" is rendered "nagagawa nang tuloy-tuloy at tama". "Tuloy-tuloy" means continuously or without stopping, not uniformly each time, so the point about skills making results repeatable gets blurred. Use "pare-pareho" or "consistent" instead. In entry [4], "code na `qiskit-ibm-runtime`" is a stiff construction, and "code ng `qiskit-ibm-runtime`" reads more naturally.

examples.source: ensure that repeatable tasks are done consistently and correctly
examples.translation: masiguro na ang mga paulit-ulit na task ay nagagawa nang tuloy-tuloy at tama
examples.suggested: masiguro na ang mga paulit-ulit na task ay nagagawa nang pare-pareho at tama
examples.why: 'Tuloy-tuloy' means continuously or without interruption, not consistently or uniformly each time. It shifts the stated benefit of skills.

examples.source: for migrating `qiskit-ibm-runtime` code
examples.translation: para sa pag-migrate ng code na `qiskit-ibm-runtime`
examples.suggested: para sa pag-migrate ng `qiskit-ibm-runtime` code
examples.why: 'code na X' reads as if the code is itself named X. The possessive 'ng' or the English word order is more natural here.

editor_note: Both rewritten headings are faithful and read naturally: "Pagmomonitor, mga calibration, at benchmarking" matches the page's own "Pagmomonitor ng parameter" and "Holistikong pagmomonitor", and "Single-qubit na performance" is a defensible heading, even though its sibling [41] is phrased as "Performance ng two-qubit".

The meaning is accurate in every entry. The C API, VF2Layout/VF2PostLayout, PauliProductMeasurement and Clifford+T claims all match the source, and nothing is added or left out. One small wording problem: entry [8] uses "gamit ang" twice in a row ("gamit ang C API ng Qiskit gamit ang bagong `QkDag` object"), which sounds stiff and like machine translation. A native editor would change the first one to "sa pamamagitan ng".

examples.source: Write custom transpiler passes through Qiskit's C API using the new `QkDag` object
examples.translation: Sumulat ng custom transpiler passes gamit ang C API ng Qiskit gamit ang bagong `QkDag` object
examples.suggested: Sumulat ng custom transpiler passes sa pamamagitan ng C API ng Qiskit gamit ang bagong `QkDag` object
examples.why: 'gamit ang' appears twice in a row. It reads as stiff machine translation, and the English uses two different prepositions here (through / using).

editor_note: All three rewritten headings are accurate and read naturally in Tagalog: "Mga standard gate" [9] matches "standard na quantum gate" in the body [10], "Mga circuit para sa pag-encode ng data" [23] is a correct native rendering, and "Mga arithmetic circuit" [39] is right, with anchors kept.

All 13 rewritten entries keep the English meaning. Option names, defaults (`"XX"`, `max_overhead` = 100), the client-side Estimator v0.50.0 noise-learning caveats for PEA and PEC, and the PEA description are all carried over intact. There is one stiff calque in entry 70: "maaaring maging sanhi ng katumpakan ng resulta na malampasan ang hiniling na katumpakan" copies the English "cause X to exceed Y" structure word for word and reads awkwardly. The meaning is still correct. Terminology is consistent throughout: "i-enable", "mga opsyon ng …", "noise model", "entangling gate".

examples.source: Note that limiting the sampling overhead can cause the precision of the result to exceed the requested precision.
examples.translation: Tandaan na ang paglilimita sa sampling overhead ay maaaring maging sanhi ng katumpakan ng resulta na malampasan ang hiniling na katumpakan.
examples.suggested: Tandaan na kapag nilimitahan mo ang sampling overhead, maaaring lumampas ang precision ng resulta sa hiniling na precision.
examples.why: This copies the English 'cause X to exceed Y' structure word for word, so the sentence reads stiffly. The meaning is preserved, so this is minor.

editor_note: Rewritten entry 4 is faithful and natural: "binuo gamit ang mga sumusunod na requirement" and "Inirerekomenda naming gamitin ang mga bersyong ito o mas bago" keep the "these versions or newer" recommendation intact, with no po/opo formality.

None of the three rewritten entries would mislead a learner, and entry 26 (the Recommendations list) is faithful and natural. In entry 6, "ay karamihan drop-in replacement" is ungrammatical because it lacks a linker, and "karamihan" ("the majority") can be read as "most of these primitives" when the English means "largely/mostly" drop-in. "halos" or "sa pangkalahatan ay" would fix both problems. In entry 5, "finer control" became "mas mahusay na kontrol" ("better control"), which loses the sense of more fine-grained control. "delegate execution" as "inililipat ang execution" is acceptable, but "ipinapasa" reads more naturally.

examples.source: these client-side primitives are largely drop-in replacements of the legacy server-side primitives
examples.translation: ang mga client-side na primitive na ito ay karamihan drop-in replacement ng mga legacy server-side na primitive
examples.suggested: ang mga client-side na primitive na ito ay halos mga drop-in replacement ng mga legacy server-side na primitive
examples.why: 'ay karamihan drop-in replacement' has no linker and reads as broken grammar. 'karamihan' means 'the majority', which can suggest only some of the primitives are replacements, when the English says they are largely interchangeable.

examples.source: faster debugging feedback, and finer control
examples.translation: mas mabilis na debugging feedback, at mas mahusay na kontrol
examples.suggested: mas mabilis na debugging feedback, at mas pinong kontrol
examples.why: 'Finer' means more fine-grained, not 'better'. The translation loses the idea of more granular control. It is a small shift that does not mislead.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries keep the English meaning, so neither would mislead a learner. In entry 13, "mga pinili nang sunod-sunod na aralin" is a clumsy rendering of "curated sequences". It reads more like "lessons picked one after another" than "curated sequences of content", and something like "mga piniling pagkakasunod-sunod ng aralin" would be clearer. In entry 12, "libreng mga alok" has the adjective in an unnatural position; "mga libreng alok" is the natural order.

examples.source: Explore curated sequences of learning, documentation, and tutorial content
examples.translation: Tuklasin ang mga pinili nang sunod-sunod na aralin, dokumentasyon, at tutorial content
examples.suggested: Tuklasin ang mga piniling pagkakasunod-sunod ng aralin, dokumentasyon, at tutorial content
examples.why: 'pinili nang sunod-sunod' reads as 'selected one after another', not as a curated sequence, so the idea of a learning path gets blurred.

examples.source: Explore our free learning offerings
examples.translation: Tuklasin ang aming libreng mga alok sa pag-aaral
examples.suggested: Tuklasin ang aming mga libreng alok sa pag-aaral
examples.why: Natural Tagalog puts 'mga' before the modifier ('mga libreng alok'). The current order sounds stiff.

editor_note: All five rewritten entries (8, 17, 35, 36, 38) keep their meaning. The "only works with" restrictions in entry 8 are both kept ("gumagana lamang"), and the v0.50.0 caveat is still there. Two small wording problems remain. In entry 8 both clauses begin with a bare code token before "ay" and have no "Ang" in front, which reads stiffly. In entry 38 "Matuto pa tungkol sa available [Mga teknik ...]" leaves "available" in English with no "na" linker, and "Mga" is capitalized in the middle of the sentence, so the line doesn't read as grammatical Tagalog.

examples.source: `NoiseLearner` only works with server-side EstimatorV2 and `NoiseLearnerV3` only works with Executor ...
examples.translation: `NoiseLearner` ay gumagana lamang sa server-side EstimatorV2 at `NoiseLearnerV3` ay gumagana lamang sa Executor ...
examples.suggested: Ang `NoiseLearner` ay gumagana lamang sa server-side EstimatorV2, at ang `NoiseLearnerV3` ay gumagana lamang sa Executor ...
examples.why: An ay-inversion subject needs the 'ang' marker. Without it, both clauses read like calqued English word order.

examples.source: Learn more about available [Error mitigation and suppression techniques](...)
examples.translation: Matuto pa tungkol sa available [Mga teknik sa error mitigation at suppression](...)
examples.suggested: Matuto pa tungkol sa mga available na [teknik sa error mitigation at suppression](...)
examples.why: The English adjective is left without a linker, and 'Mga' is capitalized inside the link in mid-sentence, so the phrase doesn't parse.

editor_note: Entries 3 and 9 are faithful and natural, with no drift. "pag-sample ng mga quantum state at pagkalkula ng mga expectation value", "mas sopistikadong implementasyon ... bilang isang cloud-based na serbisyo" and "na pinagbasehan ng IBM Quantum primitives" all keep the English meaning and use the same terms as the rest of the page.

Entry 5 is faithful and natural. "binuo gamit ang mga sumusunod na requirement" and "Inirerekomenda naming gamitin ang mga bersyong ito o mas bago" keep the "or newer" meaning and the informal register with no po/opo.

Two meaning errors could mislead a learner. First, in [25] "lamang" is attached to the probability, not the condition. The Tagalog says roughly "only a nonzero success probability was obtained when all components were enabled", which drops the English reason for the missing baseline: success happened only when full Orbit was enabled. Second, in [34] "recovered encoded state" became "nabaling encoded state", which reads as "broken/bent" (it should be "nabawing"). Smaller issues: "improvement" is rendered as "pagtaas" ("increase") in the lower-is-better error metrics ([28], [29]), while the table uses "Pagpapabuti". Other slips are "kapanatag" for "reliably", the calque "nagpapakilala" for "introduce", the ungrammatical "habang pagpapatakbo" ([13], [43]), and "sa loob ng ilang tens ng microseconds".

examples.source: no baseline improvement factor is reported because a nonzero success probability was obtained only when all Orbit components (transpilation, DD, and MEM) were enabled
examples.translation: walang iniulat na baseline improvement factor dahil isang nonzero na success probability lamang ang nakuha noong pinagana ang lahat ng Orbit component
examples.suggested: walang iniulat na baseline improvement factor dahil nakakuha lang ng nonzero na success probability kapag pinagana ang lahat ng Orbit component
examples.why: 'lamang' limits the probability instead of the condition, so the 'only when all components were enabled' logic that explains the missing baseline is lost.

examples.source: agreement between the recovered encoded state and the target logical Bell state
examples.translation: pagkakatugma sa pagitan ng nabaling encoded state at ng target na logical Bell state
examples.suggested: pagkakatugma sa pagitan ng nabawing encoded state at ng target na logical Bell state
examples.why: 'nabali' means broken/bent, not recovered, so the sentence describes the wrong state.

examples.source: The reported improvement compares the logical error probability from raw circuits to that obtained with Orbit.
examples.translation: Inihahambing ng iniulat na pagtaas ang logical error probability mula sa raw circuits sa nakuha gamit ang Orbit.
examples.suggested: Inihahambing ng iniulat na pagpapabuti ang logical error probability ...
examples.why: 'pagtaas' (increase) next to an error metric where lower is better is confusing, and it clashes with the table's 'Pagpapabuti'.

examples.source: Orbit focuses on suppressing errors during execution.
examples.translation: nakatuon ang Orbit sa pagsupress ng mga error habang pagpapatakbo.
examples.suggested: nakatuon ang Orbit sa pag-suppress ng mga error habang tumatakbo ang circuit.
examples.why: 'habang' + nominal 'pagpapatakbo' is ungrammatical (also in [43]).

examples.source: how reliably the algorithm recovers the intended solution
examples.translation: gaano kapanatag na nababawi ng algorithm ang nilalayong solusyon
examples.suggested: gaano kaaasahang nababawi ng algorithm ang nilalayong solusyon
examples.why: 'panatag' means calm/at ease, not reliable.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout. Kept terms (noise management, error mitigation/suppression, overhead, job) are consistent, and the caveat in [10] ("Hindi lahat ng opsyon ay gumagana nang magkasama...") is kept. One phrase needs fixing. In [13], "anong execution mode ang pagpapatakbuhin ng iyong job" has the wrong focus: it reads as if the job runs the execution mode. It should say the job runs in that mode: "kung saang execution mode patatakbuhin ang iyong job". Entry [0] says "Estimator primitive" on a Sampler page, but that error is in the English source and the translation copies it faithfully.

examples.source: Decide what [execution mode](execution-modes) to run your job in.
examples.translation: Magpasya kung anong [execution mode](execution-modes) ang pagpapatakbuhin ng iyong job.
examples.suggested: Magpasya kung saang [execution mode](execution-modes) patatakbuhin ang iyong job.
examples.why: The verb focus is wrong: the sentence reads as if the job runs the execution mode, not as if the job runs in that mode. It is awkward, but a reader would still get the intended meaning.

editor_note: Entry 11's Credly notice is faithful and complete: every clause is kept, including "nakabase sa Estados Unidos", the list "(pangalan, email address, at badge na natanggap)", "Maaaring ibahagi ng IBM ... sa buong mundo" with the modal intact, and both privacy-statement links.

Entry 17 matches the English clause by clause and reads naturally. It keeps the key caveats: "Maaaring ibahagi ng IBM ... sa buong mundo" preserves the "may share" hedge, and the list of shared data "(pangalan, email address, at badge na nakuha)" is complete.

The rewritten heading in entry 4 means the same thing as the English and won't mislead anyone, but it breaks the page's term convention. It says "Teoremang Espektral", a fully Filipinized form. Every other mention on the page keeps the English term "spectral theorem": the intro in entry 3 that points ahead to this section, entries 5, 24 and 25, and entry 41. The sibling headings follow the same convention ("Mga normal matrix", "Pahayag ng theorem"). So the heading should read "Spectral theorem", or at least "Teoremang spectral", so it matches the text beneath it.

examples.source: Spectral theorem {#spectral-theorem}
examples.translation: Teoremang Espektral {#spectral-theorem}
examples.suggested: Spectral theorem {#spectral-theorem}
examples.why: Within-file inconsistency: entries 3, 5, 24, 25 and 41 all keep 'spectral theorem' in English, and the other headings keep English terms ('Mga normal matrix', 'Pahayag ng theorem'). The Filipinized 'Espektral' appears only here, so the heading doesn't match the term the reader sees in the text.

editor_note: Entry 14 translates the algorithm's proper name in the heading as "Diagonalization ng Quantum na Batay sa Sample". The body right below it (entry 15) keeps "Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD)" in English, and so does the parallel SKQD heading (entry 46), so this heading is the only place the name appears translated. The wording "Diagonalization ng Quantum" also reads as "diagonalization of a quantum" rather than "quantum diagonalization", although a learner will still recognize the concept. Entry 75, "Praktis sa Programming", is faithful and natural and needs no change.

examples.source: Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization
examples.translation: Diagonalization ng Quantum na Batay sa Sample
examples.suggested: Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD)
examples.why: SQD is a proper algorithm name, and everywhere else on the page (entries 15, 46) it stays in English. Translating it only in this heading is inconsistent. 'Diagonalization ng Quantum' also turns 'quantum diagonalization' into 'diagonalization of quantum', which is slightly off.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally: [1] "Pagsusulit | Mga Pundasyon ng Quantum Business", and [12] keeps every clause of the Credly privacy notice, including "maaaring ibahagi ... sa mga third party sa buong mundo" and "Pangangasiwaan ito nang naaayon sa mga kasanayan sa privacy ng IBM".

None of the seven rewritten headings changes the meaning, and the alt text (entry 23) is fine, but two slips need an edit. Entry 41 renders the named concept "Quantum utility" as "Utility ng Quantum". That breaks up a fixed term the body keeps whole ("panahon ng quantum utility" in entry 55, "Sa pagtuon sa quantum utility" in entry 43), and it can read as "the usefulness of quantum" rather than the IBM milestone concept. Entries 21, 25, 41, 50 and 61 also switch to English-style Title Case ("Mga Superconducting Quantum Computer ng IBM", "Performance ng Quantum Computing", "Mga Supercomputer na Quantum-centric"), while the other headings on the page are in sentence case ("Pagsukat ng quantum computing performance", "Mga layunin sa pag-aaral").

examples.source: Quantum utility {#quantum-utility}
examples.translation: Utility ng Quantum {#quantum-utility}
examples.suggested: Quantum utility {#quantum-utility}
examples.why: 'Quantum utility' is a named milestone concept, and the body keeps it whole ('panahon ng quantum utility', entry 55). Splitting it into 'Utility ng Quantum' hides the term and could read as the general usefulness of quantum.

examples.source: Quantum computing performance {#quantum-computing-performance}
examples.translation: Performance ng Quantum Computing {#quantum-computing-performance}
examples.suggested: Performance ng quantum computing {#quantum-computing-performance}
examples.why: This copies English Title Case, while the neighbouring heading 'Pagsukat ng quantum computing performance' (entry 26) is in sentence case. The same applies to entries 21, 50 and 61.

examples.source: Quantum-centric supercomputers {#quantum-centric-supercomputers}
examples.translation: Mga Supercomputer na Quantum-centric {#quantum-centric-supercomputers}
examples.suggested: Mga quantum-centric supercomputer {#quantum-centric-supercomputers}
examples.why: The body keeps 'quantum-centric supercomputing' as one unit (entries 62 and 70). Moving the modifier after the noun and using Title Case makes the heading harder to match to the term in the body.

editor_note: Entry 21 renders the Credly notice faithfully, keeping every clause and caveat: "awtorisado ng IBM at matatagpuan sa Estados Unidos", the list of shared data "(pangalan, email address, at badge na nakuha)", "Maaaring ibahagi ... sa buong mundo" and "naaayon sa mga kasanayan sa privacy ng IBM". The only change is cosmetic: the full stops now sit inside the link text ("[dito.]").

None of the four rewritten entries (3, 26, 50, 60) would mislead a learner. In entry 60 the conventions note keeps its meaning: |0⟩=empty/|1⟩=occupied is still the Qiskit addons convention, and the reverse choice is still a free one. The problems are wording and consistency. The heading "Pagtupi ng Protein" (26) uses different words from the body, which says "protina" and "nagtitiklop" for folding. The heading "Transpormasyong Jordan-Wigner" (50) differs from "Jordan-Wigner transformation", which the body uses every time. Entry 60 invents the form "relumaks" and calques "one might" as "maaaring iugnay ng isa".

examples.source: Protein folding
examples.translation: Pagtupi ng Protein
examples.suggested: Pagtitiklop ng Protina
examples.why: The body text always says 'protina' and 'nagtitiklop/magtiklop' for folding. The heading uses 'Pagtupi' and the English 'Protein', so it doesn't match the section it introduces.

examples.source: Jordan-Wigner transformation
examples.translation: Transpormasyong Jordan-Wigner
examples.suggested: Jordan-Wigner transformation
examples.why: Every body mention (entries 55, 56, 73, 82, 83, 87) says 'Jordan-Wigner transformation'. The heading alone Tagalizes it, which is a within-file inconsistency.

examples.source: in the sense of an electron relaxing to the ground state of a system
examples.translation: sa diwa ng isang electron na relumaks patungo sa ground state ng isang sistema
examples.suggested: sa diwa ng isang electron na nagre-relax (bumababa) patungo sa ground state ng isang sistema
examples.why: 'relumaks' is an awkward made-up form. Native technical writing would say 'nagre-relax' or 'bumababa'. Also, 'maaaring iugnay ng isa' in the same entry is a stiff calque of 'one might associate'.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries keep the English meaning, and neither would mislead a learner. Entry 22 reads naturally ("mas malaki nang husto", "sayang lang kung susubukin na natin ngayon ang hangganan ng kaya ng VQE"). Entry 67 has one ungrammatical clause: "Maaari itong gamitin nang direkta ang Estimator" gives the verb two subjects ("itong" and "ang Estimator"). It also drops "simply", which softens the contrast in the English ("you can simply use it, but it returns much more"). The rest of entry 67 (Estimator, expectation value, cost function, ensemble standard error) matches how the file handles these terms elsewhere.

examples.source: One can simply use Estimator directly, but Estimator returns much more than just the lowest energy eigenvalue.
examples.translation: Maaari itong gamitin nang direkta ang Estimator, ngunit ...
examples.suggested: Maaaring gamitin na lang nang direkta ang Estimator, ngunit ...
examples.why: The clause has two subjects ("itong" and "ang Estimator"), which is ungrammatical. It also drops "simply", which weakens the contrast the English sets up.

editor_note: The page is faithful overall, and the key distinctions between suppression, mitigation, detection and correction survive. Two idiom slips in [5] still need fixing. "In the first place" is calqued as "sa unang pagkakataon", which reads as "the first time", and "redundantly" is rendered "nang paulit-ulit" ("repeatedly"), which blurs redundancy, the core idea of QEC encoding. The other problems are stiffness only: "mahigpit na maaaring i-verify" in [4] has awkward word order, and in [8] "bumubuo muli" ("rebuilds") stands in for "reshapes" while "strictly suppression" becomes "mahigpit na suppression".

examples.source: reduce the probability of certain errors occurring in the first place
examples.translation: bawasan ang posibilidad na mangyari ang ilang errors sa unang pagkakataon
examples.suggested: bawasan ang posibilidad na mangyari pa lang ang ilang errors (pigilan na bago pa mangyari)
examples.why: 'sa unang pagkakataon' means 'the first time', not 'to begin with'. A reader could take suppression to mean preventing only the first occurrence.

examples.source: encode quantum information redundantly across multiple qubits
examples.translation: nag-eencode ng quantum information nang paulit-ulit sa maraming qubits
examples.suggested: nag-eencode ng quantum information nang redundant (may kalabisan/duplikasyon) sa maraming qubits
examples.why: 'paulit-ulit' means repeatedly, which suggests repetition over time rather than redundancy, and redundancy is the defining idea of error-correcting codes.

examples.source: The correctness of the output can be rigorously verified.
examples.translation: Ang kawastuhan ng output ay mahigpit na maaaring i-verify.
examples.suggested: Ang kawastuhan ng output ay maaaring i-verify nang mahigpit.
examples.why: The adverb is placed before the modal, a stiff word order; putting 'nang mahigpit' after the verb reads naturally.

examples.source: reshapes noise ... rather than strictly suppression or mitigation
examples.translation: bumubuo muli sa noise ... kaysa sa mahigpit na suppression o mitigation
examples.suggested: hinuhubog muli ang noise ... sa halip na suppression o mitigation sa mahigpit na kahulugan
examples.why: 'bumubuo muli' means 'rebuilds', and 'mahigpit na suppression' calques 'strictly' as a modifier of the noun ('strict suppression').

editor_note: The rewritten heading [16] "2.2 Mapa ng coupling" means the same as the English and would not mislead a learner. The problem is consistency. The very next paragraph [17] keeps the Qiskit term as "coupling map" ("Iguguhit natin ngayon ang coupling map ng device"), so the heading and the body it introduces use different forms of the same concept. The heading should match the body's "coupling map", which is also the term learners will see in Qiskit's API and docs.

examples.source: 2.2 Coupling map {#22-coupling-map}
examples.translation: 2.2 Mapa ng coupling {#22-coupling-map}
examples.suggested: 2.2 Coupling map {#22-coupling-map}
examples.why: Entry [17], directly below, renders the same term as "coupling map". The half-translated "Mapa ng coupling" heading makes the file inconsistent, and a learner loses the direct match to the Qiskit coupling_map concept named in the section.

editor_note: All three rewritten entries are faithful: [36] keeps the "happens to have no functions" caveat as "Nagkataon namang walang functions ang Qiskit transpiler", and headings [55] "Yugto ng optimization" and [84] "Optimization ng block na one-qubit" match the file's stage→yugto convention.

None of the three rewritten headings would mislead a learner, and entry 14 ("Mga density matrix") is fine. Entries 26 and 52 are now out of step with the rest of the page. Entry 26 has "Tomograpiya ng quantum state", but the body keeps "quantum state tomography" in English (entries 27, 39, 42, 47, 51). Entry 52 has "Teleportasyon ng quantum", but every other mention on the page, including the H1 [4], subheading [54] and summary [136], keeps "quantum teleportation", and "teleportasyon ng quantum" reads as a stiff calque ("teleportation of quantum"). Changing both headings back to the English terms the page already uses would fix this.

examples.source: 4. Quantum teleportation {#4-quantum-teleportation}
examples.translation: 4. Teleportasyon ng quantum {#4-quantum-teleportation}
examples.suggested: 4. Quantum teleportation {#4-quantum-teleportation}
examples.why: Every other mention on the page keeps 'quantum teleportation' (entries 0, 4, 54, 58, 108, 136). The genitive calque 'teleportasyon ng quantum' is awkward and breaks the pattern right at the section heading.

examples.source: 3. Quantum state tomography {#3-quantum-state-tomography}
examples.translation: 3. Tomograpiya ng quantum state {#3-quantum-state-tomography}
examples.suggested: 3. Quantum state tomography {#3-quantum-state-tomography}
examples.why: The section body always uses the kept term 'quantum state tomography' (entries 27, 39, 42, 47, 51). Translating it only in the heading splits the term within the file.

editor_note: The rewritten CNOT entries (123-129) keep their meaning, including the control-on-the-right ket convention ("na ang control ay nasa kanan") and "flips when a=1". Nothing in them would mislead a learner. There are three small wording problems. In the SWAP-verification table (149), the header "Input" became "Panimula". That word means "Introduction" (it is the translation of the page's Introduction heading, entry 7), while every other truth table on the page keeps "Input". The step heading "4. Pagpoproseso Pagkatapos" (199) is a stiff calque that doesn't match its sibling headings "Pag-map", "Pag-optimize" and "Pag-execute", or the list item that keeps "**Post-processing**" (171). A smaller point: the heading "Notasyon ng vector" (86) differs from "vector notation" in the body text (91, 93).

examples.translation: | Panimula | CNOT(A,B) | CNOT(B,A) | CNOT(A,B)
examples.suggested: | Input | CNOT(A,B) | CNOT(B,A) | CNOT(A,B)
examples.why: 'Panimula' means 'Introduction' (the translation of the entry-7 heading). It is the wrong word for a column of input states and breaks consistency with every other truth table, which keeps 'Input'.

examples.source: 4. Post-processing
examples.translation: 4. Pagpoproseso Pagkatapos
examples.suggested: 4. Post-processing
examples.why: Stiff word-for-word calque ('Processing Afterward'). It doesn't match sibling steps 'Pag-map/Pag-optimize/Pag-execute' or entry 171, which keeps 'Post-processing'.

examples.source: Vector notation
examples.translation: Notasyon ng vector
examples.suggested: Vector notation
examples.why: The body text (entries 91, 93) uses 'vector notation', so the heading and the prose use different wording for the same term. Minor.

editor_note: Neither rewritten entry changes the meaning, but both break the file's own terminology convention. Entry 14 translates the list item as "Ekstrapolasyon ng zero-noise (ZNE)". Its sibling items (11-13) and every other mention (entries 5, 8, 61, 68) keep "zero-noise extrapolation" in English. Entry 34 renders the heading as "Salaming circuit", but the text around it introduces the named technique as "mirror circuit" (entries 33 and 35). "Salamin" can also mean "glass", so the heading reads oddly and no longer clearly matches the term defined in the text below it.

examples.source: Zero-noise extrapolation (ZNE)
examples.translation: Ekstrapolasyon ng zero-noise (ZNE)
examples.suggested: Zero-noise extrapolation (ZNE)
examples.why: This is the only place in the file where the technique name is translated. The other list items (Dynamical decoupling, Measurement error mitigation, Gate twirling) and all body mentions keep the English term, so this item is inconsistent.

examples.source: Mirror circuit {#mirror-circuit}
examples.translation: Salaming circuit {#mirror-circuit}
examples.suggested: Mirror circuit {#mirror-circuit}
examples.why: The technique is introduced in quotes as "mirror circuit" in entry 33 and used in English throughout entry 35. "Salaming circuit" can also be read as "glass circuit", and it makes the heading look like a different term from the one the text defines.

editor_note: None of the 8 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The headings keep their meaning, e.g. "Pinagsamang Hakbang 1-4" and "Halimbawa ng large-scale na hardware", and entry 3 keeps both the "under 30 seconds" figure and the estimate caveat. Entry 3 does slip into formal register with "inyong runtime". The page otherwise addresses the reader informally with "mo" (entry 16: "maaari mong..."), so this should be "iyong runtime" or "Maaaring mag-iba ang runtime mo". Entry 23's "Mga approach sa workflow" is an avoidable code-mix: "approach" has a common Tagalog equivalent, "paraan".

examples.source: Your runtime may vary.
examples.translation: Maaaring mag-iba ang inyong runtime.
examples.suggested: Maaaring mag-iba ang runtime mo.
examples.why: 'inyong' is the plural or formal second person. It breaks the page's casual 'mo/iyong' convention, which entry 16 already uses.

examples.source: Workflow approaches for the RZZ angle constraint
examples.translation: Mga approach sa workflow para sa RZZ angle constraint
examples.suggested: Mga paraan ng workflow para sa RZZ angle constraint
examples.why: 'approach' is an unnecessary English borrowing when 'paraan' is the natural Tagalog word. Also, 'sa workflow' reads as a calque.

editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entries 32 ("Kumpletong Grover circuit") and 39 (SamplerV2 / StatevectorSampler, "lokal na simulation") are faithful and natural. The two headings in entries 25 and 28 use the common-noun marker "ng" with a personal name: "Tiyak na instance ng Grover" and "Operator ng Grover". The rest of the page uses the correct personal form "algorithm ni Grover". Entry 28 also no longer matches the body, which keeps the named object as "Grover operator" (entries 29, 33). A native editor would write "Tiyak na instance ng Grover search" or "...ni Grover", and use "Grover operator" in the heading.

examples.source: Grover operator
examples.translation: Operator ng Grover
examples.suggested: Grover operator
examples.why: Entry 33 keeps the named object as 'Grover operator (`grover_op`)', so the heading no longer matches the body. Also, 'ng' before a personal name is ungrammatical; the page elsewhere uses 'ni Grover'.

examples.source: Specific Grover's instance
examples.translation: Tiyak na instance ng Grover
examples.suggested: Tiyak na instance ng Grover search
examples.why: 'ng Grover' treats the name as a common noun. Entry 26 says 'instance ng Grover search', so this wording is both grammatical and consistent with the body.

editor_note: None of the 8 rewritten headings would mislead a learner. They are faithful, and the Step 1–3 headings ("Hakbang 1: I-map ang mga classical input…", "I-optimize ang problema para sa pagpapatupad sa quantum hardware", "Isagawa gamit ang Qiskit primitives") match the "Hakbang N" convention used elsewhere on the page. One small issue: entry 87 renders "Dynamic MPF coefficients" as "Dynamic na mga MPF coefficient". That reads awkwardly and doesn't match its sibling heading in entry 73, "Mga static na MPF coefficient". A native editor would change it to "Mga dynamic na MPF coefficient".

examples.source: Dynamic MPF coefficients
examples.translation: Dynamic na mga MPF coefficient
examples.suggested: Mga dynamic na MPF coefficient
examples.why: Putting the plural marker 'mga' after 'Dynamic na' is awkward word order. It also breaks the pattern of the sibling heading in entry 73, 'Mga static na MPF coefficient', which a learner sees just above it.

editor_note: None of the 12 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The Step headings (Hakbang 1/2/4), the backpropagation headings and "I-transpile ang mga circuit patungo sa basis gate set" are faithful. The two section headings [26] "Halimbawa ng maliitang simulator" and [58] "Halimbawa ng malakihang hardware" attach the scale to the simulator or hardware ("example of a small simulator", "example of large-scale hardware") instead of to the example. The body text gets this right ("small-scale na halimbawa sa isang simulator" in [49]), so the headings don't match it. Heading [41] "kung gaano kalaki ang paglaki ng operator" is redundant ("how big the growth is") and drops the modal "can", so it reads stiffly.

examples.source: Small-scale simulator example
examples.translation: Halimbawa ng maliitang simulator
examples.suggested: Maliitang halimbawa sa simulator
examples.why: The qualifier describes the size of the example, not the simulator. As written it means 'example of a small simulator', which doesn't match body entry [49].

examples.source: Large-scale hardware example
examples.translation: Halimbawa ng malakihang hardware
examples.suggested: Malakihang halimbawa sa hardware
examples.why: The example is large-scale (50 qubits), not the hardware. The heading reads as 'example of large-scale hardware'.

examples.source: Constrain how large the operator can grow during backpropagation
examples.translation: Limitahan kung gaano kalaki ang paglaki ng operator habang nagba-backpropagate
examples.suggested: Limitahan kung gaano kalaki ang maaaring ilaki ng operator habang nagba-backpropagate
examples.why: 'kalaki ang paglaki' is redundant and stiff. It also drops the modal 'can', which is the sense of an upper bound.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The optimization-constraint explanation, the options description (shots, postprocessing_level, transpile_only, job_tags) and the 1→Region A / 0→Region B assignment in [53] all match the English, so nothing would mislead a learner. A native editor would still fix a few things. The region label is split: "Region A/B" in [17] but "Rehiyon A/B" in [53]. [12] uses the stiff calque "mataas-ang-taya na logistical na hamon". [17] and [19] follow English word order ("$x_j = 1$ ay itinatalaga ang market…", "Ang … constraint ay hinihiling na…") where Tagalog would put the verb first.

examples.source: A value of 1 assigns that specific market to Region A while a value of 0 assigns it to Region B.
examples.translation: …itinatalaga ang spesipikong market na iyon sa Rehiyon A samantalang … sa Rehiyon B.
examples.suggested: Use one label throughout, for example "Rehiyon A/B" in [17] as well (or "Region A/B" in both places).
examples.why: [17] says "Region A/B" and [53] says "Rehiyon A/B" for the same regions, so the label is inconsistent within the file.

examples.source: It represents a high-stakes logistical challenge
examples.translation: Kumakatawan ito sa isang mataas-ang-taya na logistical na hamon
examples.suggested: Kumakatawan ito sa isang mabigat at kritikal na hamon sa logistics
examples.why: "mataas-ang-taya" is a hyphenated word-for-word calque of "high-stakes" and reads as translationese.

examples.source: The optimization or feasibility constraint requires that the total sales allocated to Region A perfectly matches half...
examples.translation: Ang optimization o feasibility constraint ay hinihiling na ang total sales na inilaan sa Region A ay eksaktong tumutugma...
examples.suggested: Hinihingi ng optimization o feasibility constraint na eksaktong tumugma ang total sales na inilaan sa Region A sa kalahati...
examples.why: The "ay" inversion with the actor-less "hinihiling" is ungrammatical-sounding; a native writer would put the verb first and mark the constraint with "ng".

examples.source: making it challenging to find the best split using traditional exhaustive searches
examples.translation: kaya nahihirapan ang paghahanap ng pinakamahusay na split
examples.suggested: kaya mahirap hanapin ang pinakamahusay na split gamit ang tradisyonal na exhaustive search
examples.why: "nahihirapan ang paghahanap" makes the search itself the one struggling, which is an awkward personification. "mahirap hanapin" is the natural phrasing.

editor_note: Neither rewritten heading changes the meaning. Both still name the right concept, and "quantum circuit" and "loss function" stay in English as they do elsewhere in the file. The problem is that the rewrite added a leading "Ang" ("Ang quantum circuit" [37], "Ang loss function" [40]) that the English does not have. That clashes with the sibling headings in the same file, which are bare noun phrases in Title Case, like "Maliit na Halimbawa sa Simulator" [20], "Malaking Halimbawa sa Hardware" [53] and "Mga Pangangailangan" [17]. The only other heading with "Ang" is [22], "Ang max-cut problem", where the English itself says "The". Drop the article so these headings match the rest.

examples.source: Quantum circuit {#quantum-circuit}
examples.translation: Ang quantum circuit {#quantum-circuit}
examples.suggested: Quantum Circuit {#quantum-circuit}
examples.why: The rewrite adds an article the source heading does not have. That is inconsistent with the other section headings, which are bare Title Case noun phrases ([20], [53]). The meaning is unchanged.

examples.source: Loss function {#loss-function}
examples.translation: Ang loss function {#loss-function}
examples.suggested: Loss Function {#loss-function}
examples.why: Same problem: the added 'Ang' and the sentence-case capitalization break the pattern of the other headings on the page. It is a style inconsistency only and does not mislead a reader.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The postselection-rate caveat, the 16x overhead reduction, the claim that acceptance is uncorrelated with the circuit instance, and the list of possible bias sources in [45] are all rendered faithfully. In [46], "running estimate" becomes "paparating na pagtatantya" ("upcoming estimate"). It should be a cumulative or running estimate, e.g. "tumatakbong/kumulatibong pagtatantya". In [7] item 8, "far fewer shots" loses its intensifier and becomes just "mas kaunting shots", and [40] has a small tense mismatch ("nag-sample tayo ulit" is past tense for "we sample again").

examples.source: The running estimate of the site-averaged $\langle X \rangle$ as randomizations accumulate
examples.translation: Ang paparating na pagtatantya ng site-averaged na $\langle X \rangle$
examples.suggested: Ang kumulatibong (running) pagtatantya ng site-averaged na $\langle X \rangle$
examples.why: 'Paparating' means 'upcoming/arriving', not the cumulative running average the chart plots. It is recoverable from the chart context, but the wording is wrong.

examples.source: using far fewer shots than required by PEC alone
examples.translation: gamit ang mas kaunting shots kaysa sa kinakailangan ng PEC lamang
examples.suggested: gamit ang mas higit na kaunting shots (malayong mas kaunti) kaysa sa kinakailangan ng PEC lamang
examples.why: This drops the intensifier 'far', which weakens the page's main takeaway about the size of the sampling-cost savings.

examples.source: Now we sample again and include PEC randomizations
examples.translation: Ngayon, nag-sample tayo ulit at isinasama ang PEC randomizations
examples.suggested: Ngayon, magsa-sample tayo ulit at isasama ang PEC randomizations
examples.why: Mixed aspect: 'nag-sample' (completed) is followed by 'isinasama' (ongoing). Contemplative aspect reads more naturally for a step being introduced.

editor_note: All five rewritten entries (30, 42, 44, 52, 58) keep the English meaning. The condition and quantities in 58 (geometric separation ~ sqrt(N), classical complexity ~ N, quantum-projected complexity "mas maliit nang husto" than N) are intact, and the 80-minute QPU caveat and the note about provided projections in 52 are both there. The problems are small ones. In entry 52, "If you performed the training yourself" becomes "nagsagawa ng pagsasanay", but entry 46 keeps "training". "Pagsasanay" reads as "practice", so it's inconsistent and a little ambiguous in an ML context. Also in 52, "evaluated as" is rendered "suriin" ("examine") where a computation is meant, and "ay eksakto ang mga nasukat natin" is stiff. Entries 52 and 58 also keep English plural "-s" ("1-RDMs", "PQKs", "model complexities"), while the rest of the page uses "mga 1-RDM", "mga PQK".

examples.source: If you performed the training yourself, you can continue the tutorial with your own results.
examples.translation: Kung ikaw ay nagsagawa ng pagsasanay sa iyong sarili, maaari kang magpatuloy sa tutorial gamit ang iyong sariling mga resulta.
examples.suggested: Kung ikaw mismo ang nagpatakbo ng training, maaari kang magpatuloy sa tutorial gamit ang sarili mong mga resulta.
examples.why: Entry 46 keeps 'training' for the same step. 'Pagsasanay' means practice, and 'ikaw ay nagsagawa' is a stiff calque.

examples.source: the individual terms within the kernel function can be evaluated as ... These expectation values are precisely what we measured above.
examples.translation: ang bawat term sa loob ng kernel function ay maaaring suriin bilang ... Ang mga expectation value na ito ay eksakto ang mga nasukat natin sa itaas.
examples.suggested: ang bawat term sa loob ng kernel function ay maaaring kalkulahin bilang ... Ang mga expectation value na ito mismo ang sinukat natin sa itaas.
examples.why: 'Suriin' means examine or inspect, not evaluate or compute. 'Ay eksakto ang' is a word-for-word calque of 'are precisely'.

examples.source: potential advantage from the use of PQKs ... model complexities
examples.translation: potensyal na kalamangan mula sa paggamit ng PQKs ... klasikal at quantum na model complexities
examples.suggested: potensyal na kalamangan mula sa paggamit ng mga PQK ... mga model complexity ng klasikal at quantum na modelo
examples.why: English plural -s is kept here, but the rest of the page marks plurals with 'mga' ('mga PQK', 'mga model complexity' later in the same entry).

editor_note: All eight rewritten headings say the same thing as the English. "Run" and "Execute" are both rendered as "Patakbuhin" in entries 23, 25, 27 and 28, and "Step N" is used the same way in entries 14, 21, 23 and 29 ("I-map ang mga classical input…", "I-post-process at ibalik ang resulta…").

The translation is faithful overall, and the core terms stay consistent (circuit, ground state energy, Krylov subspace, i-transpile, Sampler primitive). In [15], "circuits that approximate time evolution" became "umaangkop sa time evolution", which means "adapt to" rather than "approximate". The approximation idea is lost in that sentence, though [30] and [31] ("Tinatayang", "tantiyahin") bring it back. In [46], "realized by the application of seven XXPlusYYGates" is calqued as "napagtanto", which means "came to understand", not "implemented". In [51], the gate set becomes the thing doing the decomposing, when in the English the circuits decompose into it. [38] also slips into plural/polite "kayo" in a page that otherwise uses "mo".

examples.source: this tutorial uses circuits that approximate time evolution by the Hamiltonian
examples.translation: gumagamit ng mga circuit na umaangkop sa time evolution ng Hamiltonian
examples.suggested: gumagamit ng mga circuit na tinatantiya ang time evolution ng Hamiltonian
examples.why: 'umaangkop' means adapts/fits, not approximates. The sentence loses the idea that Trotter circuits only approximate time evolution; nearby entries restore it.

examples.source: and realized by the application of seven XXPlusYYGates
examples.translation: at napagtanto sa pamamagitan ng aplikasyon ng pitong XXPlusYYGates
examples.suggested: at nabubuo sa pamamagitan ng paglalapat ng pitong XXPlusYYGates
examples.why: 'napagtanto' is a false-friend calque of 'realized' in the sense of 'understood', not 'implemented'.

examples.source: a gate set that the time evolution circuits naturally decompose to
examples.translation: isang gate set na natural na nag-decompose ng mga time evolution circuit
examples.suggested: isang gate set na natural na pinagdedecompose-an ng mga time evolution circuit
examples.why: This flips the roles: the gate set decomposes the circuits, when in the English the circuits decompose into the gate set.

examples.source: ensure that you have the following installed
examples.translation: tiyaking mayroon kayong naka-install na sumusunod
examples.suggested: tiyaking mayroon kang naka-install na sumusunod
examples.why: Plural/polite 'kayo' breaks the casual 'mo/ka' register used everywhere else in the page.

editor_note: All five rewritten entries (9, 51, 61, 62, 71) keep the meaning. The LUCJ/pass-manager explanation, the 1 mH vs 1.6 mH chemical-accuracy comparison and the noisy-QPU caveats all match the English. In entry 62, the contrastive "though" in "This is a small system, though" is dropped. "Ito ay isang maliit na sistema, at dahil…" loses the hint that the fast convergence comes with a catch, although the next sentence restores most of that caveat. Entries 51 and 62 also double the plural on English nouns, as in "mga errors" and "mga samples", which a native editor would reduce to "mga error" and "mga sample".

examples.source: This is a small system, though, and because the samples are noiseless, configuration recovery is not needed.
examples.translation: Ito ay isang maliit na sistema, at dahil ang mga samples ay walang ingay, hindi kailangan ng configuration recovery.
examples.suggested: Gayunman, maliit na sistema lang ito, at dahil walang ingay ang mga sample, hindi na kailangan ang configuration recovery.
examples.why: The concessive 'though' is dropped, which weakens the signal that the good first-iteration result will not carry over to larger systems. This is a dropped qualifier, not an inversion.

examples.source: to minimize the errors associated with the selected layout
examples.translation: upang mabawasan ang mga errors na nauugnay sa napiling layout
examples.suggested: upang mabawasan ang mga error na kaugnay ng napiling layout
examples.why: Using 'mga' with the English plural '-s' doubles the plural. Natural Taglish technical writing uses 'mga error'. The same happens with 'mga samples' in entry 62.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries match the English. Entry 7 keeps the "random-bond 156-qubit Ising model na may cubic terms" setup, and entry 32 keeps the CPLEX/Gurobi validation claim and the conditional "Kung ang algorithm ay patuloy na nakakahanap ng mas mababang costs, ipinapahiwatig nito...", so no claim is made stronger or weaker than in the source.
